reason: The cited evidence shows Mo-containing alloys (MoNbTaW, MoNbTaVW) retain high strength at elevated temperatures, but it does not directly support the specific claims that Mo addition to TiVNbTa enhances solid-solution strengthening, stabilizes edge dislocation activity, or preserves ductility. The mechanism linking edge dislocations to reduced temperature sensitivity is mentioned in E2 for a different alloy system, not for TiVNbTa with Mo.
premises: Mo addition to BCC HEAs enhances solid-solution strengthening
Mo addition stabilizes BCC structure and edge dislocation activity at high temperature
Edge dislocation activity reduces temperature sensitivity of yield strength
Mo addition will not induce secondary phases at 5–10 at.% in TiVNbTa
Mo addition improves high-temperature strength while preserving ductility
